Reflection summary: The generalizable lesson here was NOT a new arithmetic convention — the FX constant (1941 = 4.0345 USD/GBP) was already correctly captured and the forecast-chain formula (fcast = 2*Feb - Jan) was right. The recurring failure is ROW SELECTION on the late-1930s Customs trade-agreement/tariff-quota import table: "all fish commodities" is the SUM of every fish line in the group (often with no printed subtotal), and undercounting those lines produces a ~2.43x miss. I added a back-solved numeric gate (correct pct ≈ 16.13) plus a step-by-step vision-render-and-enumerate procedure so the next agent can verify before submitting.

This was an update to an existing, well-maintained reference rather than a new skill. Done — skill patched, no memory change needed (the 1941 rate and forecast-chain are already in the reference and memory is near its char cap).
